clue.text: Area in which scientist is apt to be displaying eloquence after party

definitions.text: Area in which scientist is apt to be

indicators.note: after places the eloquence piece behind the party piece in the answer

parts.note: LAB is short for the Labour Party
oratory is the art of eloquent public speaking

explanation.surface: An orator from a political party shows off a gift for fine speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs on to 'apt to be'; 'displaying' is only a link, and 'after' says the speech-making piece follows the party.
explanation.definitionFit: A laboratory is the workplace where a researcher usually carries out experiments.

clue.text: Something essentially attractive in Latin poem's sound

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem; the 's gives the S
a tone is a musical sound

explanation.surface: Someone praises the alluring sound of a Latin poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnetised piece of iron ore pulls metal towards it, so it is by its nature a thing that attracts.

clue.text: Strip players wanted?

explanation.surface: An advert seeking musicians, or a strip of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanted?' dresses the second sense as a small advert: a group of musicians sought.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip is a narrow loop or stripe of material, and players are a group of musicians performing together.

clue.text: Domestic heater painter needs help to lift over a certain height

indicators.note: in a down clue the first pieces sit over the last one

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, stands for a painter

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting the word sends it upwards, reading it from the bottom

parts.note: aid means help
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A painter needs help to raise a heater above some height.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lift' turns AID into DIA; 'over' puts RA and DIA above TOR, a rocky hilltop in the English West Country.
explanation.definitionFit: A radiator is the panel that warms a room in a home, so it is a household heater.

clue.text: Line in song, perhaps

explanation.surface: Someone points to a line in a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway line is a track, and a single song on an album is called a track.

clue.text: Plant we were very angry about

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the other

parts.note: raged means were furious

explanation.surface: Someone recalls being furious about a weed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' says the anger word wraps round 'we'; 'Plant' looks like a verb but names the weed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragweed is a wild flowering herb of the daisy family.

clue.text: Fruit tree woman left in a sorry state

indicators.note: a sorry state is a mess, telling us to jumble the letters before it

explanation.surface: A woman abandons a tree that is in a bad way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a sorry state' signals the anagram of TREE, WOMAN and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A watermelon is a large juicy melon with green rind and red flesh.

clue.text: Starveling destitute in Rialto?

indicators.note: destitute means ruined, so the word that follows is broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A starving man is penniless in Venice's Rialto.
explanation.walkthrough: Starveling is the tailor among the craftsmen in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream; 'destitute' rearranges RIALTO.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's comedy the character Starveling works as a maker of clothes.

clue.text: Cooked in salt and left in pickle?

parts.note: an old salt is a sailor, AB (able seaman)

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
cooked food is done

explanation.surface: Food prepared with salt and then preserved in brine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the cooked word inside sailor-plus-and, splitting the latter after its fourth letter. 'pickle' means a predicament, not brine.
explanation.definitionFit: To be deserted when in a mess is to be forsaken, left behind in a fix.

clue.text: Old ship, since used to carry king

indicators.note: carrying means holding something inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: ago means since then, in the past
R is short for rex, king

explanation.surface: An old vessel that has long been used to transport a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used to carry' puts R inside AGO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argo was the vessel of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth.

clue.text: Engage support of group of keen listeners

indicators.note: group of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone tries to win over an eager audience.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across keEN LISTeners.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist help is to secure backing from someone for a cause.

clue.text: Support acknowledged in French port

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: Brest is a port in Brittany
ACK is short for acknowledged, as in messaging

explanation.surface: Backing is recognised in a harbour town in France.
explanation.walkthrough: ACK is the short form of acknowledge used in signalling and computing, which many solvers will not know.
explanation.definitionFit: A backrest is the part of a chair that props up a sitter's back.

clue.text: Pooh! Pooh!

parts.note: read not as a dismissive exclamation but as two of A A Milne's bear, so a pair of stuffed toy bears

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pooh!' looks like a scornful interjection; it is Winnie-the-Pooh, a stuffed toy bear, and two of him make a plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Winnie-the-Pooh is a children's stuffed bear, so two of him are plural soft toys.

clue.text: Vegetable grown for show makes maidens quarrel

parts.note: M stands for maiden overs in cricket scoring
a quarrel is the bolt shot from a crossbow

explanation.surface: Prize vegetables at a show cause young women to fall out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarrel' looks like a row, but here it is a crossbow bolt; M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for maiden (an over with no runs).
explanation.definitionFit: Large marrows, a kind of gourd, are a classic entry in village produce competitions.

clue.text: Terribly spoiled daughter is unbalanced

indicators.note: terribly suggests the word is badly damaged, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A badly spoilt daughter is emotionally unstable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' rearranges the seven letters of 'spoiled'; the daughter's letter is then added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lopsided leans to one side, uneven in weight or shape.

clue.text: Before you put tea bag in, get sweetener

indicators.note: the bag piece is placed in front of the tea piece

parts.note: a sac is a bag-like pouch
char is slang for tea
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions for making tea: add a sweetener before the teabag goes in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before you put' places the bag ahead of the tea; char is British slang for tea, as in 'a cup of char'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saccharin is an artificial sugar substitute.

clue.text: What would make you moister -a spray?

indicators.note: make here means remake, so the letters of the words after it are formed into a new word

explanation.surface: A spray device would dampen you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'would make' rearranges MOISTER into TOMISER, with the A placed in front; the surface also describes what the device does.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomiser turns liquid into a fine mist, as in a perfume bottle.

clue.text: Kidney secretion comprehended by former Nobel prizewinner

indicators.note: comprehended means contained, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: late means former, as in the late chairman
urea is the compound the kidneys excrete in urine

explanation.surface: A medical finding about the kidney, understood by a past Nobel winner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comprehended by' means held inside; 'former' as late (the late king) is a common crossword sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A laureate is one honoured with an award, such as a Nobel.

clue.text: Greek character at Oxford is coming up to London minus tutor

parts.note: a student in residence at Oxford is said to be up

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means read from the bottom, so the word is turned round

parts.note: taken as written before being turned

indicators.note: minus is the arithmetic word for subtracting, so the tutor's letters are removed from the city name

parts.note: taken as written before the tutor is removed
a don is a university tutor

explanation.surface: A Greek student at Oxford comes to London without a tutor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns IS into SI; 'minus' takes DON from LONDON to leave LON.
explanation.definitionFit: Upsilon is the twentieth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Garrison having to keep busy

explanation.surface: Soldiers stationed somewhere must stay occupied.
explanation.definitionFit: To garrison a town is to hold it with troops, and to keep someone busy is to fill their time.

clue.text: Northern province where result's unexpected

indicators.note: an unexpected outcome is out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive is not a letter, so the word result supplies the letters

explanation.surface: An election in a northern region gives a surprise result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpected' rearranges RESULT. Ulster is the northern province of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulster is one of the four historic provinces of Ireland, in the north.

clue.text: Japanese drama doesn't play well -more than one remedy?

parts.note: Noh, also spelt No, is classical Japanese theatre
strumming a guitar is playing it casually or unskilfully

explanation.surface: A Japanese theatre performance is poorly played.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostrums are quack cures or pet solutions.

clue.text: Make an approach

explanation.surface: Someone is told to approach.
explanation.walkthrough: To run up is to make quickly (run up a dress); a run-up is the approach before a jump or a bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: To run up clothes is to sew them quickly, and a run-up is a sprinter's or bowler's approach.

clue.text: (English), pure and undefiled

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as '(English), pure and undefiled' (6), CHASTE: the opening wordplay is lost in OCR and no scan or search restores it.

clue.text: Signal student to put cigarette out?

indicators.note: out means on the outside, so the cigarette goes round the student

parts.note: fag is British slang for a cigarette
L stands for learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A signal for a student to extinguish a cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' puts FAG outside L. 'put out' looks like stubbing out the cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A flag is waved to give a signal, and to flag something is to mark it.

clue.text: Information about loch, and where it's found?

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
L is short for loch on maps

explanation.surface: A request for facts about a Scottish lake and where it lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts GEN round L; a loch lies in a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A glen is a narrow Scottish valley, where a lake typically lies.

clue.text: Divert Royal's attention for a considerable period of time

indicators.note: divert means turn aside, so the letters are redirected into a new order

parts.note: giving someone an ear is listening, paying attention

explanation.surface: Distract a royal's notice for a good long while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divert' rearranges ROYALS into SOLAR, plus Y, then EAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A solar year is the time Earth takes to orbit the Sun once, about 365 days.

clue.text: Flower Grandpa cultivated pinched by boy

indicators.note: pinched means held tight, so the boy surrounds the rest

parts.note: a son is a boy

indicators.note: cultivated means worked over like soil, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grandfather's prize flower is stolen by a lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cultivated' rearranges GRANDPA into NAPDRAG, and 'pinched by' puts it inside the boy, splitting him after his first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The snapdragon is a garden plant with dragon-shaped blooms.
